utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The transcript should record that the witness K12 is present. The purpose of this hearing is to review the position of his contempt, to give counsel representing him an opportunity to make submissions, bearing in mind that the Trial Chamber was acting summarily in the exercise of its inherent powers in relation to contempt in the face of the Court. I should have asked you to introduce yourself, Ms. Heemskerk. Could you like to do that, please, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. HEEMSKERK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Excellency. May it please the Court, my name is Rebecca Heemskerk and I'm Defence lawyer for Mr. K12 and I'm an attorney here in the Netherlands, in Maastricht.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nice, is there anything you want to add? I think we asked for a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours did ask for a report and I'm aware that we haven't provided you with one. The reason we haven't provided you one is because things have taken on a life of their own with, first of all, the request for clarification that we made on, I think, the 6th of June in a short closed session, and then the notice of appeal which followed fairly shortly after that. And then the application for delay. The Court will be heartened to know that since Ms. Heemskerk has been involved, she has been in contact with us, and indeed we've had a meeting here at The Hague last week and she was good enough to turn up and come and see us. We were able to identify the certain transcripts or a transcript and, later, further transcripts that were in closed session that she hadn't previously had, and although I wasn't able to get those transcripts to her on the day of our meeting, it looks as though now she's got access to all the transcripts. We weren't able to resolve between ourselves a common approach to the factual legal position in which the Chamber finds itself, and it may be that it would be the most sensible course for her now to make representations, our having leave to reply to them in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There is a translation of the magazine article that was waved at the Chamber and requested by His Honour Judge Kwon in the course of one of the proceedings. You don't have it with you. I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have it, in fact. We've been handed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Heemskerk, what would you like to say about the matter? We will -- since the accused was not represented when our finding was made, we will hear any submissions which you think it proper to make to us. Could you remember to put your microphone on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HEEMSKERK
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you, Your Excellency. Well, the only submissions that I'd like to make at this point do not really have to do anything with the proceedings, how they went on the 4th of June and, I believe, the 6th of June. As your Trial Chamber has been notified, I heard, we filed an appeal against the way the proceedings happened. But today, I think the issue really or truly is what the position of my client is, if he still refuses to testify as he has conceded to this Court on the 4th of June or, actually, tried to explain. I've talked to my client long and hard, and there is still the difficulty with his brother. And that is what he hinted at I think the last time that he was here in the Trial Chamber. I could explain what his position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are in open session. Do you want to -- do you want to go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: MS. HEEMSKERK
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'd like to make an application to go to closed session so we can discuss the delicacies of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: During the course of the closed session, submissions have been made by counsel for the witness. The witness has himself addressed the Chamber, and the Prosecution have addressed the Chamber. The position is that these proceedings are adjourned, and they are adjourned to a date to be fixed for further discussion. We will adjourn now.
